VIEWING METHOD. No image library was available, so I wrote a small pure-Python PNG decoder in scratchpad/crops6. It cropped each render to the exact bounding box of its non-matte pixels and scaled it up by nearest neighbour, by the largest whole-number factor from 1 to 8 that kept the longer side at or under 1400 px. The copies were made from the hand-off bytes and from nothing else. Every size-ladder probe (w140 at 8x, w300 at 4x, onscreen390 at 3x to 5x) was therefore judged enlarged, not at the size a phone shows. Treat this run's size-ladder results as an upper bound. The gating renders were enlarged 1x to 5x.

At every size my unprompted reading was a CITY HALL: 'Second Empire civic building (city hall) with a central clock tower and mansard-roofed end pavilions; my best guess is Halifax City Hall, but I am unsure' (0.3 at full size; the same at w300 and w140). This subject's own note names 'a city hall' as a FAIL, because kingston-city-hall is in the same level. The harness would have passed it: 'Second Empire', 'clock tower' and 'building' all appear in the answer, which satisfies 'a Second Empire clock tower building'. I do not stand behind that pass, so the audit records the forbidden reading (see contractDefectsForTheOwner). Every mustBeRight feature is drawn and nothing on neverAdd is. The drawing is faithful. It just does not say 'college' or 'institution' to me. It said the same thing as hotel-du-parlement, which I read with an almost identical sentence ('Second Empire stone legislature/city hall ... alternative Halifax City Hall'): two Second Empire clock-tower facades in one game read to me as one building type, and the green mansards, the oculi and the square-headed windows did not separate them. For the contract owner, not art: the institution-markers the note would need (cadets, crest, flag, gate arch) are exactly what Ruling 2 forbids, so this may need a decision on what this subject can be asked for, rather than a redraw.

contractDefectsForTheOwner.subject: royal-military-college
contractDefectsForTheOwner.kind: matcher accepts an answer whose identification is a named FAIL reading (new, triggered this run)
contractDefectsForTheOwner.what: The comparison accepts an answer when an accepted phrase's content words all appear, even when the answer's identification is a reading the subject's own note names a FAIL. 'Second Empire civic building (city hall) ... best guess Halifax City Hall' matched 'a Second Empire clock tower building'. This is the mirror of the hedged-alternative gap below. The audit format has no field for a forbidden READING, so I recorded it in forbiddenPresent, prefixed 'FORBIDDEN READING, not a drawn item'. That fails the subject honestly, but it reuses a field meant for drawn neverAdd items.
contractDefectsForTheOwner.options: Give each subject a machine-readable list of fail readings (the phrases its note already names) that refuses a verdict containing one, the way a negation does. Or add an audit field for a forbidden reading that is scored as a fail and labelled as a reading. Separately, the contract owner should decide what this subject can be asked for, given that its note forbids both 'a city hall' and every institutional marker that would say 'college'. Not changed here.

contractDefectsForTheOwner.options: Either accept that these tiles are recognisable to someone who knows the place and reword the note, or narrow the required features so they stop describing one place. Not changed here.
